stories.title: Push Notification Delivery via APNs and FCM
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to receive push notifications about location-based offers on my device so that I am alerted to relevant deals nearby.
acceptance_criteria: Given a consumer has a registered device token, When a notification is triggered, Then the system delivers the push via APNs (iOS) or FCM (Android) within 5 seconds
Given a notification delivery fails, When the failure is transient (timeout/5xx), Then the system retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff
Given a device token is invalid or expired, When delivery fails with a permanent error, Then the token is marked inactive and no further attempts are made
Given multiple notifications are queued, When batch sending is triggered, Then notifications are sent in batches of up to 500 via platform-native batch APIs
Given the notification contains offer data, When delivered, Then the payload includes offer_id, merchant_name, short_description, and deep_link URI
Security: Given device tokens are stored, When at rest, Then they are encrypted using AES-256 via Cloud KMS (CMEK)
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Pub/Sub for async messaging, GKE for container orchestration, Memorystore (Redis) for caching, Secret Manager for secrets
stories.reasoning: Core infrastructure story enabling all notification delivery. APNs/FCM integration is foundational. Retry logic and batch sending ensure reliability at scale for 10M+ mobile users.

stories.title: Notification Preference Controls
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to control when and how I receive offer notifications so that I only get alerts that suit my lifestyle.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the notification preferences screen, When I view the options, Then I can select from 'Always', 'App Open Only', or 'Off' delivery modes
Given I set quiet hours, When a notification is triggered during my quiet period, Then it is suppressed and not queued for later delivery
Given I toggle category preferences, When I disable a category (e.g., dining), Then I no longer receive notifications for offers in that category
Given I change a preference, When I save, Then the change takes effect within 10 seconds for subsequent notifications
Accessibility: Given I am using a screen reader, When I navigate the preferences screen, Then all controls have accessible labels, roles, and states conforming to WCAG 2.1 AA
Accessibility: Given I am using the preferences screen, When I interact with toggles, Then focus order is logical and state changes are announced to assistive technology
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards, Consumer Duty compliance, shared design system component library
stories.reasoning: Consumer Duty requires clear, accessible controls for communication preferences. Quiet hours and category toggles give granular control, reducing notification fatigue and opt-outs.

stories.title: Notification Frequency Capping
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to be protected from excessive notifications so that the offers I receive feel valuable rather than intrusive.
acceptance_criteria: Given I have already received a notification for a specific offer today, When the same offer triggers again, Then no duplicate notification is sent (1 per offer per day cap)
Given I have received 5 notifications today, When a 6th is triggered, Then it is suppressed (5 total per day cap)
Given I received a notification less than 30 minutes ago, When another is triggered, Then it is held until the 30-minute gap has elapsed
Given frequency cap state is stored in Redis (Memorystore), When the Redis instance is unavailable, Then the system fails closed (suppresses the notification) and logs the error
Given a new day begins (midnight UK time), When the daily counters reset, Then the consumer can receive notifications again from 00:00 GMT/BST
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Memorystore (Redis) for caching, fail-closed security posture
stories.reasoning: Frequency capping is critical for Consumer Duty compliance and user retention. Redis provides sub-millisecond lookups for real-time cap enforcement. Fail-closed ensures over-notification never occurs on infrastructure failure.

stories.title: User Profile & Spending Preferences Setup
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to set up my spending preferences and profile so that the offers I receive are personalised to my interests and budget.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am setting up my profile, When I enter my display name, Then it is stored and shown on my profile (max 50 characters, alphanumeric and spaces only)
Given I am selecting spending categories, When I choose from the available list, Then I can select multiple categories (e.g., dining, groceries, fashion, travel, entertainment)
Given I am setting budget sensitivity, When I choose a level (low/medium/high), Then offers are filtered to match my price sensitivity
Given I am setting my preferred radius, When I select a distance (0.5km, 1km, 2km, 5km), Then only offers within that radius trigger notifications
Given I have not completed profile setup, When I access the offers feature, Then I am prompted to complete setup with the option to skip

Accessibility: Given I am using the profile setup screen, When I interact with form fields, Then all inputs have visible labels, error messages are programmatically associated, and the form is navigable via keyboard
Security: Given profile data is stored, When at rest, Then it is encrypted and access is restricted to the user's authenticated session only
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Cloud SQL for relational data, encryption at rest AES-256, OAuth 2.0/OIDC for auth, WCAG 2.1 AA
stories.reasoning: Personalisation preferences drive offer relevance. Budget sensitivity and radius settings directly impact notification targeting quality. Data minimisation (GDPR Art.5) requires collecting only what's needed.

stories.title: Push Permission Pre-Permission Screen
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to understand why the app needs push notification permission before being asked so that I can make an informed decision.
acceptance_criteria: Given I have not yet granted push permission, When I first access the offers feature, Then a pre-permission screen explains the value of notifications with clear benefit messaging
Given the pre-permission screen is displayed, When I tap 'Enable Notifications', Then the native OS permission dialog is presented
Given the pre-permission screen is displayed, When I tap 'Not Now', Then the OS dialog is not shown and I can proceed to use offers without push
Given the pre-permission screen is displayed, When I view it, Then it includes an illustration/icon, a headline, 2-3 bullet benefits, and two action buttons
Accessibility: Given I am using a screen reader, When the pre-permission screen is displayed, Then all content is readable, buttons have distinct accessible names, and focus is managed correctly
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) apps, shared design system, WCAG 2.1 AA
stories.reasoning: Pre-permission screens significantly increase opt-in rates (industry data: 2-3x). Consumer Duty requires informed consent. This avoids burning the one-time OS permission prompt on an unprepared user.

stories.title: Push Permission Denial Handling & In-App Fallback
stories.user_story: As a consumer who has denied push permissions, I want to still see relevant offers within the app so that I don't miss out on deals.
acceptance_criteria: Given I have denied push notification permission, When I open the app, Then I see an in-app notification badge/banner for new offers
Given I have denied push permission, When I navigate to the offers section, Then new offers since my last visit are highlighted with a 'New' indicator
Given I previously denied permission, When I visit notification preferences, Then I see a non-intrusive prompt explaining how to re-enable push via device settings with a deep-link to OS settings
Given the re-enable prompt has been dismissed, When I return to preferences, Then the prompt is not shown again for 30 days
Accessibility: Given in-app fallback notifications are displayed, When a new offer badge appears, Then it is announced to assistive technology via a live region
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Native iOS/Android apps, WCAG 2.1 AA, Consumer Duty customer outcomes focus
stories.reasoning: Users who deny push must still receive value from the offers feature. In-app fallback ensures no user is excluded. The 30-day re-prompt cooldown respects user choice per Consumer Duty.

stories.title: Quiet Hours Configuration
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to set quiet hours during which no notifications are sent so that I am not disturbed during sleep or personal time.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the notification preferences screen, When I enable quiet hours, Then I can set a start time and end time using a time picker
Given quiet hours span midnight (e.g., 22:00–07:00), When a notification is triggered at 23:30, Then it is suppressed
Given quiet hours are active, When a notification is suppressed, Then it is discarded (not queued) to avoid morning notification floods
Given I have not set quiet hours, When the feature is first available, Then a sensible default of 22:00–07:00 is suggested but not enforced
Accessibility: Given I am using the time picker, When I interact with it, Then it supports both touch and keyboard input with clear time format labelling (HH:MM, 24-hour)
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Consumer Duty customer outcomes, shared design system component library
stories.reasoning: Quiet hours are a key Consumer Duty control preventing notifications at antisocial hours. Discarding rather than queuing prevents morning notification floods which would undermine the feature's purpose.

stories.title: Device Token Registration & Lifecycle Management
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want my device to be automatically registered for push notifications so that I receive offers without manual setup.
acceptance_criteria: Given I grant push permission, When the OS returns a device token, Then it is sent to the backend and stored against my user profile
Given I have multiple devices, When I log in on a new device, Then the new device token is registered alongside existing tokens
Given a device token is refreshed by the OS, When the app detects the new token, Then it updates the backend registration
Given I log out of the app, When the session ends, Then the device token association is removed (token is not deleted but disassociated)
Security: Given device tokens are transmitted, When sent to the backend, Then they are transmitted over TLS 1.3 and stored encrypted at rest
Security: Given the token registration endpoint exists, When a request is received, Then it requires a valid OAuth 2.0 bearer token
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: TLS 1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest, OAuth 2.0/OIDC auth, Cloud IAM
stories.reasoning: Device token lifecycle management is essential for reliable delivery. Multi-device support reflects real user behaviour. Disassociation on logout prevents notifications to shared/sold devices.

stories.title: Frequency Cap Error Handling & Observability
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want the notification system to handle errors gracefully so that I never receive a flood of notifications due to a system failure.
acceptance_criteria: Given Redis (Memorystore) is unreachable, When a notification is triggered, Then the system suppresses delivery and emits a critical alert to Cloud Monitoring
Given a frequency cap check times out (>100ms), When the timeout occurs, Then the notification is suppressed and the timeout is logged with trace context
Given the frequency capping service recovers after an outage, When normal operation resumes, Then daily counters reflect only notifications actually delivered (no phantom counts)
Given frequency cap decisions are made, When each decision occurs, Then a structured log entry is emitted with user_id (hashed), offer_id, decision (allow/suppress), and reason
Given operational metrics are collected, When viewed in Cloud Monitoring, Then dashboards show suppression rate, Redis latency p99, and error rate per 5-minute window
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging (structured), Cloud Trace, Prometheus, Memorystore (Redis)
stories.reasoning: Error path story ensuring system resilience. Fail-closed prevents notification floods. Observability via Cloud Monitoring/Logging aligns with Lloyds' confirmed observability stack and PRA operational resilience requirements.

stories.title: Spending Preferences Update & Data Privacy
stories.user_story: As a consumer, I want to update or delete my spending preferences at any time so that I remain in control of my personal data.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the profile screen, When I modify any preference (categories, budget sensitivity, radius), Then the change is persisted and reflected in offer targeting within 30 seconds
Given I want to reset my preferences, When I tap 'Reset to Defaults', Then all preferences return to system defaults and a confirmation is shown
Given I want to delete my profile data, When I request deletion via the privacy settings, Then all spending preference data is permanently deleted within 72 hours per UK GDPR Art.17
Given I delete my preferences, When deletion is complete, Then I receive a confirmation and the system falls back to generic (non-personalised) offer delivery
Security: Given preference data is accessed via API, When a request is made, Then the API validates that the authenticated user can only access their own data (no IDOR vulnerability)
Accessibility: Given I am on the profile screen, When I trigger the reset action, Then a confirmation dialog is focus-trapped and announced to screen readers
stories.citation: Lloyds EA KB: UK GDPR/DPA 2018/DUAA 2025 compliance, OAuth 2.0 auth, Cloud SQL
stories.reasoning: GDPR rights (rectification Art.16, erasure Art.17) must be implemented. IDOR prevention is critical for multi-user systems. The 72-hour deletion window aligns with ICO guidance on erasure timelines.

coverage_matrix.coverage_notes: Covers APNs/FCM delivery, retry logic, batch sending, device token lifecycle, and security controls
Covers delivery mode selection, category toggles, quiet hours configuration with accessibility
Covers per-offer, daily, and gap caps via Redis plus error handling and observability
Covers profile setup, category/budget/radius preferences, GDPR data rights, and security
Covers pre-permission UX, denial handling, in-app fallback notifications, and re-enable prompting

regression_summary: No regression criteria applicable — greenfield epic with no existing functionality to protect. All stories introduce new capabilities. Integration regression points to monitor in future sprints: (1) Push delivery pipeline end-to-end after preference changes, (2) Frequency cap accuracy after Redis failover, (3) In-app fallback rendering after push permission state changes, (4) Profile data deletion completeness verification.
